newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain to remain vigilant on prices, wages.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain to remain vigilant on prices, wages.

text.p: The Bank of Spain's monetary policy will remain vigilant in 1997 over inflation and wages' growth, the central bank's 1997 report said on Tuesday.
The Bank of Spain's 1997 inflation target was set at around 2.5 percent, with the medium term target set at around 2.0 percent in 1998.

"To produce this reduction in the inflation trend, wages have to grow in a coherent way and the (likely) improvement in economic fundamentals should not be taken advantage of...to increase company's unit margins," the report said.
Imported inflation from rising oil prices might also be a risk, the report added.
Under these circustances the Bank of Spain's aim would be to avoid "an acceleration of prices that may cause the (inflation) targets to be missed".
